I-001.threat: Side-channel key extraction — attacker extracts cryptographic keys via side-channel analysis
I-001.cause: No side-channel countermeasures — cryptographic operations leak key-correlated signals
I-001.attack: Attacker measures power or EM emissions during cryptographic operations to extract secret keys

I-002.threat: Firmware extraction via debug readback — attacker reads firmware through debug interface
I-002.cause: Debug interface accessible and readback protection not enabled
I-002.attack: Attacker connects to unlocked debug interface and reads complete flash contents

I-003.threat: Embedded storage information disclosure — attacker reads sensitive data from non-volatile memory
I-003.cause: Flash/EEPROM/NVRAM lacks readback protection — stored keys and credentials are readable
I-003.attack: Attacker reads non-volatile memory to extract firmware, cryptographic keys, or sensitive configuration

I-004.threat: Shared-memory residual data exposure — secrets remain readable in volatile shared memory after use
I-004.cause: Shared-memory region is not cleared after use — sensitive data persists between tasks or cores
I-004.attack: A second core or a later task reads stale buffer contents (keys, plaintext) left in the shared region

I-005.threat: Memory isolation bypass (read) — protected region readable across privilege domains
I-005.cause: The MPU/MMU region for the shared memory or MMIO block is misconfigured — isolation between domains is not enforced
I-005.attack: A low-privilege task or peripheral reads a memory region it should not reach, extracting secrets or sensor data
